Definition: strictly a demonstrative particle, here; but used of time, now or then
BiblicalUsage: Ephow is a small word for then, now, so — the word that turns a sentence into a question or a plea. Isaac trembles and asks, who then is he that hath taken venison; Moses asks, wherein shall it be known then that I have found grace; Job cries, Oh that my words were now written.
TheologicalSignificance: Then is when the truth lands, and now is when the cry goes up, and this little word carries the weight of the moment.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
